actions: 1. Conduct a rapid field walk to identify symptoms of Anthracnose, powdery mildew, or nutrient deficiency on leaves and fruits.
2. Increase drip‑irrigation flow to deliver an additional 10‑15 mm of water per week for the next 2 weeks, adjusting emitters to ensure uniform wetting of the root zone.
3. Apply a split dose of NPK 10:10:10 (or equivalent) at 150 kg ha⁻¹, split into two applications 7 days apart, starting today.
4. Spread a 5‑cm layer of well‑decomposed compost or farmyard manure around the tree drip line to raise organic carbon and act as mulch.
5. Install simple soil moisture sensors (tensiometers or capacitance probes) at 30 cm depth to verify irrigation effectiveness.
6. Record all actions in a field log with dates, quantities, and observations.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored canopy vigor (NDVI >0.45) within 3 weeks, reduced water stress, minimized disease incidence, and improved soil organic carbon, leading to preservation of current fruit set and positioning the crop for a profitable harvest during the May‑July window.

• Bi‑weekly visual disease scouting, focusing on leaf spots and powdery growth.
• Daily observation of soil moisture sensor readings; maintain field capacity above 25 %.
• Soil organic carbon test after the next rainy season (≈6 months) to assess mulching impact.
• Market price watch: confirm price trends remain upward before harvest.
